1.1.text:
Article 3

1. The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
2. Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF SINTANG REGENCY

NUMBER 8 OF 2015

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY

REGENT OF SINTANG,

Considering:

a. that all forms of acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights so that their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination; b. that in addition to protection efforts, prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children victims of violence are needed, so as to achieve the fulfillment, advancement, enforcement and protection of human rights universally and fundamentally; c. that in connection with the intention in letter b and in an effort to provide a legal basis for its implementation in Sintang Regency, it is necessary to regulate the protection of women and children victims of violence; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation of Sintang Regency concerning Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence; In View of:

1. Law Number 27 of 1959 concerning Stipulation of Emergency Law Number 3 of 1953 Concerning Establishment of Level II Regions in Kalimantan (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1953 Number 9, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 352) as Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1959 Number 72, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 1820); 2. Law Number 1 of 1974 concerning Marriage (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1974 Number 1, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3019); 3. Law Number 4 of 1979 concerning Child Welfare (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1979 Number 32, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3143); 4. Law Number 8 of 1981 concerning Criminal Procedure Law (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1981 Number 76, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3209); 5. Law Number 8 of 1999 concerning Consumer Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 42, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3821); 6. Law Number 20 of 1999 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 138 Concerning Minimum Age For Admission To Employment (ILO Convention Concerning Minimum Age For Admission To Employment) (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 56, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3835); 7. Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 1999 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3886); 8. Law Number 1 of 2000 concerning Ratification of ILO Convention No. 182 Concerning The Prohibition And Immediate Action For The Elimination Of The Worst Forms Of Child Labour (ILO Convention No. 182 concerning The Prohibition And Immediate Action For The Elimination Of The Worst Forms Of Child Labour) (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2000 Number 30, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 3941); 9. Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2002 Number 109, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4235) as amended by Law Number 35 of 2014 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 297, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5606); 10. Law Number 13 of 2003 concerning Manpower (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2003 Number 39, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4279); 11. Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2004 Number 95, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4419); 12. Law Number 13 of 2006 concerning Protection of Witnesses And Victims (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2006 Number 64, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4635) as amended by Law Number 31 of 2014 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 293, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5602); 13. Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4720); 14. Law Number 12 of 2011 concerning Establishment of Legislation (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2011 Number 82, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5234); 15. Law Number 11 of 2012 concerning Juvenile Justice System (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2012 Number 153); 16. Law Number 23 of 2014 concerning Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2014 Number 244, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5587) as amended by Law Number 9 of 2015 (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2015 Number 58, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 5679); 17. Government Regulation Number 79 of 2005 concerning Guidelines for Development And Supervision of Regional Government Administration (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2005 Number 165, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4593); 18. Government Regulation Number 38 of 2007 concerning Division of Government Affairs Between the Government, Provincial Regional Government And Regency/City Regional Government (State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia of 2007 Number 82, Supplement to the State Gazette of the Republic of Indonesia Number 4737); 19.

Article 20

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
3. The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

CHAPTER XII

OTHER PROVISIONS

Article 21

Further provisions regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is an act based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.

Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

CHAPTER VIII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 16

1. Guidance on the implementation of protection for women and children is carried out by relevant Agencies in accordance with their respective main duties and functions.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) is in the form of providing guidelines that include technical implementation of protection for women and children.
3. Supervision of the implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by relevant Agencies together with internal government supervisory apparatus in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER XI

CRIMINAL PROVISIONS

Article 19

Every criminal act relating to the protection of women and children shall be subject to criminal sanctions as stipulated in applicable laws and regulations.

Article 2

Letter a
Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

Letter b
Gender justice is a state where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to obtain opportunities (access), as well as welfare.

Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

Article 10

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A of Sintang Regency receives case referrals from service institutions in the Sintang Regency area.
3. Provisions regarding P2TP2A are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 11

1. The principle of service implementation for victims is not charged any fees whatsoever.
2. The implementation of services for victims is carried out quickly, safely, with empathy, and non-discriminatory.
3. Services for victims regarding everything reported are guaranteed confidentiality.

Article 3

1. The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
2. Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

CHAPTER XII

OTHER PROVISIONS

Article 21

Further provisions regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 20

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
3. The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.

30. Article 3

1. The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.

b. sexual violence; and/or

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 20

1. 2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).

What is meant by gender-based violence is an act based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.

Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.

16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 20

1. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Letter b
Gender justice is a state where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to obtain opportunities (access), as well as welfare.

Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is an act based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.

Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 3

What is meant by gender-based violence is an act based on gender relations that places women in a subordinate position to men.

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.

Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.

Article 2

Letter a
Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

Letter b
Gender justice is a state where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to obtain opportunities (access), as well as welfare.

Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 20

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
3. The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

Article 8

The Manager of Women and Children Protection implemented by P2TP2A has the obligation to organize services in accordance with service principles as regulated in this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Article 11

1. The principle of service implementation for victims is not charged any fees whatsoever.
2. The implementation of services for victims is carried out quickly, safely, with empathy, and non-discriminatory.
3. Services for victims regarding everything reported are guaranteed confidentiality.

Part Two

Implementation Principles

Article 10

1. The implementation of protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner within the framework of P2TP2A.
2. P2TP2A of Sintang Regency receives case referrals from service institutions in the Sintang Regency area.
3. Provisions regarding P2TP2A are further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Institutional

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

Article 20

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
3. The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

Article 2

Letter a
Respect for the rights of victims is intended to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of victims as referred to in Article 5.

Letter b
Gender justice is a state where every person, both men and women, is treated equally and obtains equal opportunities to obtain opportunities (access), as well as welfare.

Gender equality is equality of rights, opportunities, benefits and decision-making between women and men including in entering employment opportunities both in the formal and informal sectors.

Letter c
Non-Discrimination is an attitude and treatment towards victims by not making distinctions based on age, gender, race, ethnicity, religion and between groups.

Letter d
The best interests of victims are all best actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, so the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration.

Part Three

Forms and Mechanisms of Service

Article 8

The Manager of Women and Children Protection implemented by P2TP2A has the obligation to organize services in accordance with service principles as regulated in this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER IX

ADMINISTRATIVE SANCTIONS

Article 17

1. Officials or Officers appointed by authorized institutions/agencies who fail to carry out obligations and responsibilities as stipulated in Article 7 and Article 8, shall be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. written warning from the authorized official; and/or
b. fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Further provisions regarding the procedures for imposing administrative sanctions as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be stipulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

Sufficiently clear

Article 4

The provision of services to victims is carried out with principles including free of charge, fast, safe, empathetic, non-discriminatory, easily accessible, and confidential.

Article 4

Sufficiently clear.

Article 6

Sufficiently clear.

Sufficiently clear.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

30. Forms and Mechanisms of Service

Article 4

Obligations and Responsibilities of the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment

Article 3

1. The purpose of Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is to provide protection and services for the best interests of women and children victims of violence occurring in the domestic and/or public sphere.
2. Forms of violence against women and children as referred to in paragraph (1) include among others:
a. physical violence;
b. sexual violence; and/or
c. psychological violence.

Article 20

1. Any person who intentionally fails to provide protection to women and/or children resulting in the occurrence of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (2), allows violence to occur, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
2. Any person who obstructs officers or the P2TP2A institution or any party in making efforts to protect and provide services for women and/or children victims of violence as referred to in Article 3 paragraph (1), shall be punished with imprisonment of at most 6 (six) months or a fine of at most Rp.50,000,000.00 (fifty million rupiah).
3. The criminal act as referred to in paragraph (1) is a violation.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Sintang Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of the regional government administration.
3. Regent is the Regent of Sintang.
4. Woman is a person of female gender.
5. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those in the womb (who are not married).
6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

From the series of provisions above, the Government is responsible for taking actions both legally, politically, economically and socially to prevent, suppress, reduce and eliminate all forms of violence against women and children because this constitutes a crime against human existence.

I. GENERAL

The State has an obligation to provide a sense of security to its citizens from threats and actions that can disturb or damage mental, physical, sexual or economic security, this philosophy is stated in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution that the purpose of establishing the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, the first is to protect the entire nation and all of Indonesia's homeland.

Furthermore, in the National Action Plan for the Elimination of Violence Against Women Year 1999 it is stated that Women as mothers of the nation and children as assets and successors of the nation are creatures created by Almighty God so they must be protected and their honor, dignity and self-respect must be maintained properly and proportionally, both legally, economically, politically, socially and culturally, without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race and class.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

1. Region is Sintang Regency.

6. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, social, psychological to the victim.
7. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in public or private life.
8. Violence against children is any act that results in suffering of children physically, sexually, economically, socially and psychologically.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.
11. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, court, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
14. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will occur, is occurring or has occurred.
16. Companion is a person or representative from an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
17. Judicial body is the general judiciary that has the authority to receive, examine, and adjudicate, as well as resolve every case submitted to it, to realize law enforcement and justice.
18. Prosecution is the action of the public prosecutor to transfer a case to the competent district court in the manner and according to the procedures regulated in the law with a request that it be examined and decided by a judge in a court session.
19. Lawsuit is a notification accompanied by a request by an interested party to a judge to take action according to law against a person who has harmed him/her in a civil manner.
20. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a service provider institution for victims of violence based at the Regional General Hospital managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medicolegal), psychosocial and legal services.
21. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
22. Standard Operating Procedure hereinafter abbreviated as SOP is the standard operating procedure that serves as a reference for service actions established by Regent Regulation.
23. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or community organizations.
24. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, and mother and children.
25. Household is family members and relatives (grandchildren, nephews/nieces, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
26. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Sintang Regency.
27. Prosecutor's Office is the Prosecutor's Office of the Republic of Indonesia, which is a government institution that exercises state power in the field of prosecution and other authorities based on law.
28. Police is all matters relating to the functions and institutions of the police in accordance with statutory regulations.
29. Advocate is a person who carries out activities related to facilitating and fighting for the rights and obligations of clients/persons based on applicable regulations.
30. Social Worker is a profession whose main field is engaged in organized social service activities, where these activities aim to provide facilities and strengthen relations, especially in mutually beneficial and reciprocal adjustment between individuals and their social environment through the use of social work methods.
31. Psychiatrist is a specialist doctor profession who has specialization in the diagnosis and treatment of emotional disorders.
32. Visum et Repertum is a statement given by a Doctor regarding matters required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.
33. Visum et Repertum Psikiatrikum is a statement given by a Psychiatric Medicine Expert Doctor regarding the mental health condition of a person required to clarify a criminal and civil case for the purposes of examination.

Domestic sphere means the space where interpersonal relations occur.

Public sphere means the space where relations concerning public interests occur.

Service and assistance institutions must also be able to provide education and awareness to the community about such gender-based violence.
